results.notes: Outcome is reader-rated paragraph_clarity on the original 0-100 scale. Treatment is Reranking (model_mitigation_condition='reranking'); control is No Intervention ('none'). Data mapping and exclusions were established by the main paper, supplement Sections 5.2/8.5, and the authors' R files read as text only. Within writer_id/proposition_id, use paragraph_type='edited' when available, otherwise 'model'; exclude both AI and human paragraphs when writer_preference='original'. The edited subset has 23,412 rating rows; the preferred subset has 19,102 (9,576 unaided, 3,262 none, 3,179 prompting, 3,085 reranking), from 730 distinct writers and 2,543 readers. It includes 648 control and 603 treatment writers before restricting to paired or first-round samples. Each writer has one task per condition; ratings are averaged within writer/condition with equal weight per writer. The reproduction entries concern the published full-sample preferred-subset regression, before complete-pair or first-round restriction. Reproduction independently maximizes the reader-random-intercept beta-regression Laplace likelihood after transforming y to ((y/100)*(N-1)+0.5)/N; AMEs use inverse-logit predictions with reader effect set to zero. Analytic likelihood gradients were checked by central differences. The supplement is dated 2026-10-08 and titled 'How AI writing assistance distorts perceptions of AI users and their opinions', while the saved main paper is arXiv:2604.22503v2 dated 2026-06-29. For these Study 3 outcomes, sample, intervention, reader-only model, and the main-paper clarity percentage agree; newer Study 1 specifications are not substituted. Supplement PDF p. 200, Table S287, supplies numeric AMEs/odds ratios for this outcome. The requested computed fields are raw participant-level outcome levels and treatment-minus-control differences in rating points, not the paper's normalized attenuation percentage. No unaided baseline is subtracted from these computed fields. SDs use denominator n-1. Preference exclusions follow the paper and are post-treatment selection, so these are conditional-sample contrasts rather than intention-to-treat estimates. The printed -26.9 percent is reproduced as 100*(AME_reranking-AME_none)/AME_none; independently computed value=-26.8602655788. Paired analysis retains only writers with both eligible conditions. Difference is mean(treatment_i-control_i); SE is SD(treatment_i-control_i)/sqrt(n). Both condition SDs are across this identical set of paired writers.
